review_notes: I read Foundation.lean and Separation.lean in full, plus active, activeCore and HasFiniteWitnesses in Basic.lean. I found no other repeated-machinery findings. exists_countable_same_core and setSeparates_iff_countable are one-off arguments, and setSeparates_finset is a short unfolding. I did not run Lean, so the rewrites are untested.

claims.reason: The two proofs repeat the same nontrivial argument. Forward direction: finiteWitnesses_iff_separating (Separation.lean lines 43-56) and valid_iff_positive_separates (Foundation.lean lines 40-47 and 57-58) both take S := hC.toFinset and prove every L in F lies in active H T S. Both then contradict infinitude of activeCore via hC.subset. Backward direction: both prove ⋂₀ active H T S = activeCore H T S, apply the separation hypothesis to active H T S, and close with hK.2.2 (hL.2.1 hx). Positivity is used in neither direction. HasFiniteWitnesses (Basic.lean 53-56) is ∃ T, positivity and the core condition, which matches Valid H T. Foundation imports Separation, so the lemma must live in Separation.lean, which creates no cycle. Both theorems then become short wrappers and the substantive argument is maintained once. Caveat: Separates is stated with Generic.LanguageClass and Generic.Language, while Foundation uses Set (Set α) and Set α. They appear to unfold to the same types, but I did not check the definitions.
claims.shared_lemma: theorem activeCore_infinite_iff_separates (H : Generic.LanguageClass α) (T : Generic.Language α → Finset α) : (∀ S : Finset α, (active H T S).Nonempty → (activeCore H T S).Infinite) ↔ Separates H T
rewritten_uses: finiteWitnesses_iff_separating: constructor; · rintro ⟨T, hpos, hcore⟩; exact ⟨T, hpos, (activeCore_infinite_iff_separates H T).mp hcore⟩; · rintro ⟨T, hpos, hsep⟩; exact ⟨T, hpos, (activeCore_infinite_iff_separates H T).mpr hsep⟩
valid_iff_positive_separates: exact and_congr_right (fun _ => activeCore_infinite_iff_separates H T), since Valid H T unfolds to Positive H T ∧ ∀ S, ...
